inbound_admission.rs module doc claims SocketMessage has no hop_chain (false since D532)
description:
crates/ganja-serve/tests/inbound_admission.rs's module doc states that
SocketMessage carries no hop_chain field, and therefore that the guard's hop
drops (HopLoop / HopRunaway) cannot be driven from the HTTP layer. Both
halves of that went false on 2026-08-27 with D532 (commit d1e9727): the
envelope now carries hop_chain (parse-bounded at 32) alongside message_id,
from_mode and reply_to, and W3 (commit 999a168) made the socket route
destructure and forward every one of them into the gate — so a hop-loop or
hop-runaway drop IS now drivable end to end through POST
/team/{name}/message, with the answer asserted byte-identical to an accept.

Why the fix was excluded from that landing rather than done inline: the
plan's AC-39 confines crates/ganja-serve/ to exactly three paths
(src/routes.rs, src/lib.rs's crate doc, tests/team.rs). Editing this file
would have added a fourth ganja-serve path and broken the confinement
evidence the landing's own verification bundle rests on. The W3 lane found
it, the lead adjudicated it out, and this is where it went.

TWO PIECES OF WORK, the first required and the second optional:
1. REQUIRED — correct the module doc sentence. It is now actively
   misleading: a reader planning hop-guard coverage will conclude from it
   that the HTTP layer cannot reach those arms.
2. OPTIONAL — add the HTTP-layer hop-drop cases the corrected sentence
   makes possible. Engine-level coverage already exists
   (crates/ganja-core/tests/peer_envelope.rs), so these would pin the ROUTE
   forwarding rather than the guard: that a chain arriving over HTTP reaches
   PeerGuard::admit intact, that a looping chain is dropped before any entry
   enters the hold buffer or any Event::PeerHeld is raised, and that the
   dropped answer is byte-identical to an accept.

Anchor: crates/ganja-serve/tests/inbound_admission.rs, module doc.

title: D530/D531 teamless surface is reachable in no shipped binary: make teamless a live has-no-team state, or delete SoloPostbox and teamless_send
description: Found 2026-08-29 while deciding ganja-code-e99 (the no-config-home arm), by code trace. Every shipped interactive non-member session takes ganja-tui/src/lib.rs's Some(home) arm: TeammateRegistry::for_session names the team session-<8hex> (teammate.rs:511 session_team) and Engine::with_teammates installs the LEAD postbox (engine.rs:2041 install_postbox), which stamps from = <name>@session-<hex> (subagent.rs:1148) and stores teamless=false. The solo machinery is built in exactly two places: the dead leaf lib.rs:504 (engine.with_solo_postbox) that D542/e99 deletes, and Engine::retire_team (engine.rs:2560), production-callerless. Consequences in every shipped binary: (1) from is never <name>@solo and ONE_WAY_NOTE (subagent.rs:2212) is never appended — D530's identity clause has no production witness; (2) Engine::teamless (engine.rs:1236) is never true, so session.rs:3866 effective_default never returns Ask — D531's teamless_send: "ask" config key never has an effect, though it is curated, schema'd and documented as putting a dialog in front of each send_message; (3) team_messaging (engine.rs:4532) never selects SendMessageTool::teamless(), so TEAMLESS_DESCRIPTION (send_message.rs:130) is never shown; the model sees the team description over an empty roster. Decide between: (A) MAKE IT LIVE — derive teamless from has-no-team (registry holds no members; a team whose members all left is teamless again, F10's own rule) so teamless_send and the teamless description take effect on the real path, keep from = <name>@session-<hex> on the wire (a session that binds a socket IS addressable, so @solo + one-way would be false), delete SoloPostbox/ONE_WAY_NOTE/retire_team; amends D530's identity clause, makes D531 true. (C) LEAVE — documented as engine-tested seams (what D542 does), dead code the next reader sizes against. Also carry e99's open observation (b): can a registry-legal but MemberName-illegal self-name (my-app.v2) receive through the TEAM path? title: Split the mcp table into .mcp.toml
description:
Deferred follow-up from the TOML config migration (.omc/plans/2026-08-28-toml-config-migration.md, ADR Follow-ups). The migration was held to a strict 1:1 translation — same keys, same tiers, same semantics, one format — so that the only thing under review was the format change itself. Splitting the mcp table into its own .mcp.toml is a separate decision and was deliberately not prejudiced by it.

Two arguments carry the split:

1. The D462 collision dissolution. Top-level keys that logically belong to a table are currently hoisted out of it precisely to avoid colliding with a user-chosen name inside it: tool_defer_threshold is top-level because a defer_threshold key inside [mcp] would collide with a server actually named that, which is the same lesson agents.concurrency learned against an agent named concurrency. A file whose whole content is the mcp table has no such collision to dodge, so those hoisted keys could return to where they belong.

2. Machine-writer separation. ganja mcp add/get/remove is a machine writer editing a file humans hand-comment. Today it edits the one config file through toml_edit's CST specifically so the human's comments, ordering and formatting survive (D483, D536). A dedicated .mcp.toml would put the machine-written table in a file of its own, which is the same separation Claude Code's own .mcp.json makes and the reason that file exists there.

Open questions this issue must answer before any code: whether .mcp.toml is discovered in the same three tiers as ganja.toml and how it merges with an mcp table still present in the main file (both, or refuse one); whether the split is additive or a second clean cut; what ganja mcp add writes when neither file exists; and whether the schema splits with it.

crates/ganja-tool/src/list_sessions.rs: a resident, argument-free tool
answering one formatted listing rather than raw records, in two labeled
sections. Teammates comes off the Postbox roster this crate already
exposes, with the lead marked as that roster marks it — and the section is
left out rather than printed empty where the roster is, since a roster
cannot tell a lead of nobody from a session with no team. Live sessions
comes off registry.rs's own records, composed in holders' own
drop-own-then-probe-only-matches order rather than list + probe-everything,
because is_live CREATES the .lock it opens and probing every record would
litter one beside every name in the directory. This session is excluded, so
is a stale lock-free record, and every row prints name, stem, cwd and the
exact uds: spelling — which makes "a duplicate name shows its stem" true of
every row rather than a special case (D528's ratified disambiguator).

The trust story this bead asked for, answered: each live row carries the
same unverified label the mention reminder carries on the same bytes (a
session's name is that session's own choice and nothing verifies it), and
registry text is neutralized before rendering — reproduced locally rather
than shared, because ganja-tool's internal dependency list is asserted to
be exactly `ganja-permission ` and the reminder's neutralization lives in
ganja-core.

The permission posture, decided with evidence rather than assumed:
UNASKED. `read` and `glob` are unasked and can already read
/tmp/ganja-<uid>/*.json directly, so an ask would gate a formatted view of
data the model can already fetch unformatted. A deny rule still denies.

Liveness is the resolver's vocabulary and not the CLI lister's — the lock
probe alone, the same test the resolver re-applies the moment the model
addresses a printed row — because this crate may not link ganja-client and
a model-cadence tool must not open a connection per session; the honest
cost (a bound but wedged session lists as live) is in the tool's own
description.

Registration gate, deliberately NOT send_message's: send_message is offered
on postbox presence alone, list_sessions only where the installed postbox
can actually cross a session — so a pane member, whose MemberPostbox
refuses Address::Uds outright, keeps send_message and is offered no
listing. Also landed with it: send_message's teamless description no longer

title: ganja run <msg>: when stdin is a non-TTY pipe that is never closed (a wrapper/harness holding it open), piped_stdin() blocks forever in read_to_string before the turn starts — even though a message was given on the command line; `</dev/null` is the workaround
description: Found 2026-08-20 while probing meridian from the Claude Code Bash tool: `ganja run --format json "..."` hung 5 min with no step_start and no log line; `sample` showed run::piped_stdin -> Stdin::read_to_string -> read(2). run.rs:1074 reads stdin to EOF whenever it is not a terminal, unconditionally, then resolve_input() merges it with the argv message — so a harness that keeps stdin open as a pipe (this Bash tool, some CI runners, tmux send-keys'd wrappers) wedges the run. Upstream opencode's run.ts has the same shape (reads stdin when !isTTY). Options: (a) only read piped stdin when no argv message was given (or when --stdin is passed); (b) read with a short non-blocking probe / poll(2) for readability and treat 'nothing ready' as no pipe; (c) keep parity and document `</dev/null`. Decide against upstream parity (D-ledger) before changing.

description:
FILED, NOT ACTED ON. The honest treatment of this may be DELETION rather
than completion, and that is exactly why it needs a decision instead of a
patch.

THE FINDING (code trace, 2026-08-27, run twice — once by the closing
landing's planner, once independently by its architect review).
config_home() answers None IFF GANJA_CONFIG_HOME is unset (or blank after
trimming) AND Xdg::new() errs — one deterministic call over $HOME. But

Project::data_dir calls data_home(), which calls THE SAME Xdg::new():

  - crates/ganja-tui/src/lib.rs:211-213   (229 lines BEFORE the assembly
                                           match at :442 that selects the

  - crates/ganja-cli/src/assemble.rs:62-64
  - crates/ganja-cli/src/main.rs:1663-1666 (`sessions`)

The one Xdg::new() failure tolerated on the startup path is the log
directory (main.rs:1031-1037), which routes through declined() and prints a
note.

THEREFORE: in every shipped binary, the condition that selects the
no-config-home assembly arm is a condition in which the process has already
exited. The arm is STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE, not merely rare.

WHAT IS DEAD BEHIND IT: the production install of SoloPostbox
(with_solo_postbox on that arm), ONE_WAY_NOTE (subagent.rs ~:2196, applied
~:2327) — a sentence no user has ever read — and the solo machinery around
them. They are exercised only by engine/testkit assemblies that bypass
run().

WHY IT WAS NOT ACTED ON. Root AGENTS.md records the solo machinery under
D530 as "the engine-tested spelling of the teamless contract", and D530 is
USER-RATIFIED (2026-08-26, ratified against the plan's own recommendation).
Deleting it reopens a landed decision on evidence that arrived after it.
The closing landing therefore ruled OQ1(b) — leave the predicate alone,
build nothing behind it, fix the sentences — and filed this rather than
folding deletion into an option.

THE THREE THINGS A DECISION MUST WEIGH:
1. DELETE. Two arms instead of three, so the bind predicate reads once
   because there is nothing else to read; ONE_WAY_NOTE goes with it. Cost:
   reopening D530, and losing the tested spelling of a contract.
2. FINISH. Build the receiving surface behind it (peer view, recipient

   ten acceptance criteria for a code path that cannot execute — the
   arithmetic that moved the closing landing's recommendation to (b).
3. LEAVE IT. Today's state. Cost: dead code the next reader will size work
   against, exactly as the closing landing's own plan nearly did for two
   revision rounds while AGENTS.md said "near-unreachable in practice".

TWO EXECUTION OBSERVATIONS THAT BELONG HERE:
(a) ONE_WAY_NOTE is applied UNCONDITIONALLY at its site, and it is true in
    every shipped build only because the solo arm binds nothing. A testkit
    fixture that pairs a solo postbox with a bound socket makes it
    OBSERVABLY FALSE — the sentence is a property of the assembly, not of
    the postbox, and nothing in the type system says so. Whichever way this
    is decided, that coupling should be made explicit or removed.
(b) OPEN QUESTION, unanswered: can a registry-legal but MemberName-illegal
    name — `my-app.v2`, which vet_name admits and MemberName's
    ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ refuses — receive through the TEAM
    path today? The closing landing's AC-15 was written for the solo path
    and the solo path was not built, so the question was never driven. If

    is a bug independent of everything above.

core: recompose_tools composes over the already-composed set, so a composition can add a tool but never remove one
description: Found by l-3tng while landing D543 (2026-08-30). Engine::recompose_tools composes over the *already composed* tool set rather than from the lent base, so a composition step can add a tool (send_message, list_sessions) but never take one away; ganja-core/tests/session_listing.rs::installing_a_member_postbox_over_a_lead_takes_the_listing_away only passes because a later refresh_team rebuilds from the lent set (rebuild_offered(lent, shape)). Fix: make recompose_tools rebuild from the lent base (the way refresh_team does) so composition is idempotent from a fixed input, and pin it with a test that installs a postbox kind that cannot cross-session send after one that could and asserts the listing tool is gone without a refresh_team in between. notes: review-3tng confirmed the diagnosis in the live tree (engine.rs ~:4638-4641 recompose_tools calls self.compose(self.tools(), …) — input is the composed set, Registry::with can only add or replace by id; rebuild_offered ~:4384 composes from lent and is the only path that removes). Scoping note before building anything: the replace_* seams and the /plugin Reload already go through rebuild_offered, so first confirm there is a reachable caller that relies on recompose_tools alone to WITHDRAW a tool — the gap may be narrower than the asymmetry suggests.

title: a bind opt-out that actually unbinds (backlog)
description:
BACKLOG — filed so the one real worry the closing landing could not answer
is on the record, not because it should be built.

cross_session_inbound: "refuse" is this build's decline, and it is honest
about what it does: the drop happens AFTER admission, so the socket stays
bound, the process still accepts connections, the registration record stays
on disk, and the session keeps appearing in `ganja sessions --live`, in
another session's @ menu and to D528's resolver. That is the reference's own
administrative distinction and it is why listings stay truthful.

A user whose actual worry is a BOUND SOCKET has no switch in this build.
Not a hypothetical worry: the socket takes no credential, and same-uid is
explicitly not trusted here — ganja-permission's whole premise is that code
this user runs (an MCP server, a hook, the model's bash) is not the user.
"Refuse" answers "do not deliver to me". It does not answer "do not listen".

Why this is a regression to build carelessly, and therefore backlog rather
than ready: a key that unbinds takes a session OUT of sessions --live, out
of the @ menu's live-session rows, out of D528's resolver (which reads the
records these sessions write) and out of D529's mention renderings — i.e.
it rolls back landed D527-D529 behavior for whoever sets it. The closing
landing considered it as its first open question's option (c), labelled it a
regression rather than "the smallest exposure", and did not take it.

If it is ever wanted, it needs its own plan, and that plan must answer:
what the OTHER sessions are told when a name they can see stops resolving;
whether an unbound session still writes a record (it must not, or the
listing lies); and whether the key is per-project or global, since a
project file may only TIGHTEN cross_session_inbound and the same rule would
have to hold here.

title: replace_base_tools and refresh_mcp can interleave now that Engine seams are &self

Before the L4 Mutex-ification (&mut self via &mut App) the frontend serialized them; now the engine is Arc-shared with the session socket and a peer's POST /session/{id}/message (routes.rs:82) can start a turn — hence refresh_mcp — concurrently with the TUI thread's /plugin Reload. Self-heals at the next reload or MCP generation bump. Needs a manual /plugin Reload racing a wire-driven turn start whose MCP generation just moved; no panic/data loss/credential exposure; TurnSlot still prevents two root turns. Fix options: fold both bodies' base->lent transition under one mutex, or recompute lent from base_tools() inside the same critical section.

Why it matters: the codex backend decides a feature cohort from originator + User-Agent + version. The current recording says the honest name costs that seat nothing. A version bump changes one of those three inputs, and nothing in CI would notice a demotion.
## Acceptance-2 grep is CODE-SCOPED — do not "fix" the docs to satisfy it

When re-probing, the plan's acceptance criterion 2 must be read code-scoped:

    grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'opencode/1.18' crates/

own test assertions), auth/copilot.rs, provider/copilot.rs.

Why the flag matters: the per-host identity tables in AGENTS.md and
crates/ganja-provider/src/AGENTS.md legitimately QUOTE the borrowed value, in
order to say which hosts receive it. An unscoped grep therefore also matches
documentation. r2 ruled the criterion passes on intent — no code site outside
those three files names the borrowed UA — and the tables are the intended

comments.text:
2026-08-27 — REASON REWRITTEN, STAYS OPEN. The closing cross-session
landing (D532-D535) found this bead's stated reason wrong — not its
conclusion.

Old reason: "ganja serve leads no team today, so a serve-led session
registers nothing." That is a fact about serve but it is not the test.
Since D505 the bind gate has been "locates a config home and is not a pane
member", never "leads a team" — a session with no teammates at all binds,
registers and receives — so "leads no team" was never what kept serve out.

New reason, and it is a stronger one: a serve-led session has no PEER DRAIN
and no HOLD-REVIEW SURFACE. Binding a socket makes a session addressable,
and a message that lands in an inbox nothing drains is a message the sender
was told arrived and nobody will ever read; a hold that raises no dialog and
appears in no /held listing and on no status segment is a message parked
where no person can release it. ganja-serve drives the engine but renders
no transcript, drains no peer batch, and surfaces no permission or held
dialog of its own — those live in ganja-tui. That, and not the team
question, is the test a session must pass before it may advertise an
address. It is the same test that keeps headless `ganja run` unbound (a
bound inbox nothing drains is a black hole, worse than an honest refusal).

Note also what did NOT change: under the user's OQ1(b) ruling the bind
predicate is unchanged and no receiving surface was built for a teamless
session, so nothing in D532-D535 moved serve closer to registering. If serve
ever grows a drain and a review surface — the day it leads teams, or the day
someone gives its HTTP surface a held-dialog road — the record lifecycle it
needs is the TUI's, already written: one writer per record, removal before
the socket stops answering, collision notice surfaced wherever serve
surfaces notices.

comments.author: zchee
comments.text:
2026-08-27 — LANDED as D534 (commits d945f42 W2, 999a168 W3), unblocked by
D532's reply_to.

What shipped, against what this bead asked for. A settlement rides back to
a reply-capable sender over a fourth socket route, POST /peer/receipt on
the SENDER's socket — and ONLY a held message's settlement ever does. An
accept emits nothing, a refuse emits nothing, a guard drop emits nothing,
which is what keeps D523's byte-identical answer structural rather than
asserted: no receipt's presence or absence can tell an accept from a
refuse. The held fact itself was already answered synchronously on the POST
that was held, and now says so with a typed SocketDelivered.held field
rather than in the note's prose, so an outstanding id is registered only
when the answer said held AND a reply address rode along — silence on the
route therefore means exactly one thing, still held.

Trust: nothing. Three admission tests (id must be outstanding; any of the
three statuses removes the entry; the route answers identically admitted or
dropped), a 200-id registry evicted oldest-first and cleared by NewSession.
A forged receipt can lie about one known message's fate and nothing else.

Receiver side: exactly three emitting paths — a person releases, a person
denies, the dialog_expiry clock fires — so Expired means the review window
ran out and nothing else. A capacity eviction emits nothing (evicts with no
person involved, at an attacker-chosen rate once the buffer is primed) and
the shutdown drain emits nothing (a hundred settlements at once to
sender-chosen addresses inside a 750 ms teardown budget, and a crash
settles nothing at all). Senders those paths cannot reach are left "true
and stale", the same place a crash already leaves them.

Also landed with it: the guard's checks hoisted ahead of the hold arm,
scoped by cause to the two parity causes this landing newly aimed traffic
at, so hold generation is rate-limited while a configured
cross_session_inbound: "hold" keeps reaching the review surface its owner
asked for; the HeldId association living in receipts.rs's own map, leaving
HeldMessage byte-untouched; and the model-facing half as one
<peer_receipt>-tagged part on D529's vehicle plus one status-bar line

title: Put a screenshot or GIF of the TUI in the README
design:
For a terminal UI project the screen is the highest-converting element a README can carry, and this one has none while its tagline says ganja lives in your terminal.

Candidates, in rough order of how well they show what is distinctive: the transcript rendering with the Claude Code grammar ported in D487 (the bullet, result and thinking markers), the /team dialog with a member's ring of recent calls, or the compaction gauge mid-turn.

Drive the capture with the fake provider rather than a live one: GANJA_FAKE_SCRIPT points at a JSON script of thinking, text and tool calls per turn, so the recording is deterministic and can be regenerated identically later. That matters because a screenshot committed today will eventually be re-shot against a changed UI, and a reproducible driver is the difference between re-shooting and re-staging.

The asset gets committed, so choose format and size deliberately -- a GIF of a streaming turn is large, and a still of the settled transcript may carry the grammar just as well at a fraction of the bytes.

title: Adoption drops no own marker: a peer can poison this session's own-marker count for one cell
description:
Parity security review §1 (2026-08-27) proposed three clauses for the adoption clamp; clause 2 (drop this session's own marker before storing the adopted chain) was RULED OUT and the grounds are in teammate::inbound::adoptable_chain's doc.

Reason: the own-marker count climbs only because each forwarder leaves its marker in the chain. A session that stripped its own on every adoption would hold a two-cycle at constant length forever (V appends V, W adopts and strips nothing, W appends W, V adopts and strips V, ...) and MAX_SELF_HOPS would never fire for any participant. The check's usefulness is worth more than the residual below.

Residual, unclosed by design: a peer may send a chain carrying up to MAX_SELF_HOPS (10) of this session's own marker — one more is refused as HopLoop before adoption sees it — so this session's forwards then carry 11, and a message routed back here is dropped as a loop. It lasts only until the next admitted inbound or a NewSession replaces the cell.

Any future fix must not be an unconditional strip. Candidates worth weighing: making the chain per-message rather than per-session, or clamping the adopted own-marker count to something below MAX_SELF_HOPS while still letting it climb.

Pinned by an_adopted_chain_keeps_this_sessions_own_marker (crates/ganja-core/src/teammate/inbound_tests.rs), which reddens if somebody adds the strip.

title: serde type-mismatch messages quote the rejected config value
description: Found while landing the parse-error fix (MINOR-3). `located()` stops the *line* from being reproduced, which was the finding; it does not stop serde's own message from naming the single value it rejected — "invalid type: string \"…\", expected a boolean". That is one value rather than every value sharing its line, it is what makes the message actionable, and it predates the TOML change: serde_json behaves identically, so the JSONC reader in config::legacy always did this too. Recorded rather than fixed because suppressing it would leave a type error nobody can act on. Scope is documented in the doc comments on both `located` helpers (ganja-cli/src/position.rs, ganja-core/src/config.rs).
notes: Reviewer qualification (2026-08-28, series close): the residual is narrow TODAY because of a property of the current type surface, not a design guarantee. Every field where a credential actually lives — McpLocal::environment, both headers maps, provider.key_env, LspEntry::env — is String or BTreeMap<String, String>, so a type mismatch there prints the wrong value the author typed, never a token beside it; a token can only appear in an 'invalid type' message if somebody typed it into a non-string field. The day a non-string field is added that could plausibly hold credential-adjacent text, this becomes live and nothing in the tree will flag it — re-evaluate then. deny_unknown_fields messages enumerate known field names and the offending key only, never values.

title: provider: responses.rs module doc says 'none of the three headers' where four are sent
description:
r2's finding 5 from the final review of .omc/plans/2026-08-25-ganja-code-identity-headers.md.

crates/ganja-provider/src/provider/responses.rs's module doc describes what a key request does NOT gain. The extra-headers table row now lists four (ACCOUNT_HEADER, ORIGINATOR_HEADER, BETA_HEADER, CODEX_USER_AGENT) and the prose beside it was reworded to "none of the four headers the subscription branch adds", but a nearby sentence still says "three".

Why this was not simply bumped to four during D521 — the same reasoning as ratified deviation (c), and the reason this is a bead rather than a one-character edit: the sentence cites `codex.ts:405-408`, and that line range in the pinned checkout is the header-COPY LOOP. Upstream sets `authorization` at :410 and `ChatGPT-Account-Id` at :412; the originator is at :551; BETA_HEADER is not from the pin at all (its own doc says so). So "none of the four headers `:405-408` set" would be a FALSE CITATION — worse than a stale count, because a reader who follows it finds nothing and cannot tell whether the code or the citation drifted.

title: provider: retry.rs truncates before redacting — a spilled body could be cut mid-credential
description:
Residue from r1's W2 review of .omc/plans/2026-08-25-ganja-code-identity-headers.md. Production seam, cheap fix.

The ordering is the defect: a body is truncated and then redacted, so a credential straddling the cut can leave its head in the kept half with nothing left to match on. Redaction that runs after truncation is matching against a string the truncation already damaged.

Current mitigation, and why this is not urgent: tests/codex_identity_probe.rs asserts on a prefix rather than a whole value, so the probe path does not depend on the tail surviving. That is a property of one test, not of the seam.

Fix direction: redact first, then truncate — so what is cut is already masked, and a partial match cannot become a partial leak.

Distinct from ganja-code-ccs, which is about WHICH credential the mask covers (key_env vs a token in a config headers entry). This one is about ORDER, and the two want fixing together since both live in the same masking path.

trailing-punctuation mention tokens (@name, stays literal)
description:
An @-token followed by punctuation — "@backend, can you look at this" —
does not classify as a session mention: the trailing comma is part of the
token, no name matches it, and the whole thing stays literal. The closing
cross-session landing (D532-D535, 2026-08-27) hit this at its submit
classifier (Axis 14) and filed it rather than fixing it.

Why it was not fixed there. The rule is not the session classifier's; it is
the FILE mention scanner's token rule (crates/ganja-tui/src/mention.rs), and
both scanners share it. Changing it for session tokens alone splits one
mention grammar into two, which is a worse defect than the hole. Changing it
for both is a mention-grammar change with its own blast radius: @file#5-9
line ranges live inside the same token, so whatever strips a trailing comma
has to not strip a range, a trailing '#', or a path whose last character is
legitimately punctuation.

What a fix would need:
- One rule, applied at one place, for both file and session tokens.
- An explicit list of what may be stripped from the tail and what may not,
  with the #<digits>[-<digits>] range shape excluded by construction (the
  same shape D527's name grammar refuses at the other end, so the two stay
  consistent).
- Snapshot coverage for the existing file-mention cases first, so the
  regression surface is visible before the rule moves.

Symptom to reproduce: type "@<a live session name>, hello" and submit; the
token stays literal and no <session_mention> part is composed.

title: pane members as addressable receivers (Axis 6e)
description:
A pane teammate binds no socket and is not name-addressable from outside its
own team; the closing cross-session landing (D532-D535, 2026-08-27) recorded
that as a deliberate absence rather than an omission, and this bead carries
the reopening.

Two arguments keep it out today, and both would have to be answered:

1. AUTHORITY. A member's human authority is its lead. Its permission dialogs
   already travel to the lead as §5's permission_request, and the lead's own
   §6.2 pass is where a person sees what a member is doing. A direct inbox
   routes around that pass — a third session could put words in front of a
   member's model without the lead ever seeing them.
2. IT COULD NOT ACT ON THE ANSWER ANYWAY. MemberPostbox::deliver refuses
   Address::Uds outright (Undelivered::NoTransport) and resolves an
   Address::Local name only against its own team file — no registry read, no
   resolver, no socket. This is the same fact that keeps D535's
   list_sessions out of a pane member: a member cannot cross a session in
   either direction.

So this is not a one-line gate change. Making a member addressable means
deciding what a peer message to a member IS with respect to its lead
(carried through the lead? surfaced in the lead's ring? invisible?), and
whether the same session should also gain a cross-session send — which is
what would make the D535 listing worth offering it too. Design it as one
question, not two.

Prerequisites already in the tree: the D523-D525 admission gate is
frontend-generic (hold dialog, /held listing, N held segment all work in
whatever frontend runs the engine), and D532's envelope carries a reply
address, so receipts would work for a member the day one binds.
